$comment: Source of truth for the security-linting skill. Every package, preset key and rule name here is locked against the plugins' own exports by scripts/__tests__/security-linting-skill.lock.test.ts. `dependencies` and `dependencyPrefixes` match a project's package.json (dependencies, devDependencies, peerDependencies, optionalDependencies); `fields` matches a top-level package.json field. A plugin is added when ANY signal matches. `always` plugins are added to every project. `recommendedIsExactly` is set only where the recommended preset is exactly that rule list.

baseline.why: The established baseline, kept as is. The plugin's own README warns it produces many false positives that need human triage.

plugins.why: Framework-agnostic injection (LDAP, XPath, XXE, GraphQL, template), hardcoded credentials, unsafe deserialization, ReDoS, fail-open auth.
plugins.limits: Pattern rules inside one file, not taint tracking across files. detect-object-injection and detect-non-literal-regexp exist but are not in recommended.

plugins.why: Node runtime: child_process and shell injection, path traversal, SSRF, weak crypto and hashes, TLS verification off, Buffer misuse, zip slip.
plugins.limits: For code that runs on Node. It does not apply to code that only runs in a browser.

plugins.why: Express: helmet and CSP, CORS, cookies, CSRF, rate limiting, open redirects, error leakage, body-parser limits.
plugins.limits: Express only. Fastify and Koa have no plugin of ours.

plugins.why: NestJS: guards, ValidationPipe and its whitelist, throttling, CORS, serialization of private fields, multer uploads.
plugins.limits: Guards and pipes registered globally in another file are found by a text scan of the project, not by type analysis, so a global guard can be missed or over-trusted.

plugins.why: Browser: innerHTML and eval sinks, postMessage origin checks, tokens in localStorage, cookie attributes, insecure WebSocket and URLs.
plugins.limits: DOM and Web API patterns. It does not flag React's dangerouslySetInnerHTML (that is react/no-danger from eslint-plugin-react, or no-danger in our eslint-plugin-react-features).

plugins.why: JWT: the none algorithm, missing algorithm allowlist, decode without verify, hardcoded or weak secrets, missing expiry.
plugins.limits: Checks how tokens are signed and verified in your code. It does not check key management or claims at runtime.

plugins.why: PostgreSQL drivers: SQL built from strings, TLS verification off, hardcoded credentials, unsafe COPY and search_path, pool misuse.
plugins.limits: Only files that import one of those drivers are checked. recommended also holds non-security hygiene rules at warn (no-select-all, no-batch-insert-loop).

plugins.why: mysql and mysql2: SQL built from strings.
plugins.limits: One rule at recommended.

plugins.why: MongoDB and Mongoose: NoSQL operator injection, $where, regex DoS, hardcoded connection strings.
plugins.limits: Query-shape patterns in your code, not schema or index review.

plugins.why: SQLite drivers: SQL built from strings.
plugins.limits: One rule at recommended.

plugins.why: Knex: SQL built from strings in raw queries.
plugins.limits: One rule at recommended.

plugins.why: Prisma: SQL built from strings in raw queries.
plugins.limits: One rule at recommended.

plugins.why: Drizzle: SQL built from strings in raw queries.
plugins.limits: One rule at recommended.

plugins.why: Sequelize: SQL built from strings in raw queries.
plugins.limits: One rule at recommended.

plugins.why: TypeORM: SQL built from strings in raw queries.
plugins.limits: One rule at recommended.

plugins.why: Supabase: service_role key in client code, dynamic rpc names, unchecked auth errors.
plugins.limits: Client-code patterns. Row-level security policies live in your database and are not linted.

plugins.why: gRPC: server reflection registered with no guard publishes every service on the listener; a caller identity read from metadata lets any client claim to be anyone.
plugins.limits: Identity is reported only when it meets an equality check against a per-request record, in the same file.

plugins.why: MCP servers and clients: tool arguments reaching eval, shell, SQL, fs or fetch, session ids, transport hardening, tool-description injection.
plugins.limits: Targets the @modelcontextprotocol SDK packages. Other MCP implementations are not claimed.

plugins.why: OpenAI SDK: a literal API key, or dangerouslyAllowBrowser exposing it.
plugins.limits: Two rules at recommended. Prompt-injection handling is not at this preset.

plugins.why: Anthropic SDK: a literal API key, or dangerouslyAllowBrowser exposing it.
plugins.limits: Two rules at recommended.

plugins.why: Gemini SDK: a literal API key, or harm-category filters switched off.
plugins.limits: Two rules at recommended.

plugins.why: Vercel AI SDK: unvalidated prompts, AI output reaching eval/SQL/HTML, secrets in prompts, missing tool schemas and limits.
plugins.limits: Static patterns around the SDK calls. It cannot judge whether a prompt is actually safe at runtime.

plugins.why: AWS Lambda: hardcoded credentials, wildcard CORS, secrets in env, user-controlled request URLs, over-broad IAM policy literals.
plugins.limits: Handler and policy-literal patterns in code. Deployed IAM and infrastructure templates are not scanned.

notCovered: Vulnerable dependencies (use npm audit, osv-scanner or your SCA tool).
Secrets already committed to git history.
Runtime behaviour, authorization logic and business-logic flaws.
Taint tracking across files: rules look inside one file, plus the project-level scans noted per plugin.
Fastify, Koa and Hapi application rules, and any framework not in the table.
Some rules skip files under test, fixtures, mocks or similar directories by design (nestjs-security does), so a proof file must not live there.
